correctness.rationale: Any row-column, row-symbol, or column-symbol pair has one Latin completion. With at most three previous distinct elements, a new distinct choice either has no incidence constraint, tests one completion, or tests two distinct completions. In the one-completion case the old diagram tells whether that completion is already chosen; in the two-completion case the possible vectors are (1,0), (0,1), (0,0). With just two previously named elements of different sorts, not explicitly separated in the proof's case split, both incidence and nonincidence are available in the third sort. At orders at least four there is always a fresh choice when required. This yields the four-move strategy. Normalization forces the squares of orders 1–3, and existential row counts distinguish the resulting classes. The separator has depth five, not six: the two symbol quantifiers occur on separate branches below four outer quantifiers. The cited C4 witness gives diagonal 0,0 and off-diagonal 3,1, while characteristic two forces off-diagonal equality in V4. The bundled source and recorded outputs are consistent with this argument; the argument does not depend on running them.
residual_risks: This proves the stated two-square separation, not a general rank-five classification or a transfer to multiplication or graph languages.

originality.rationale: The distinct Resultary record dated 2026-10-26 explicitly gives both main claims in the identical signature, including the same rank-five separating property. Neither the alternate proof presentation nor finite corroboration adds a distinct finding. This is demonstrated equivalent coverage, not a claim about ultimate historical priority.
residual_risks: Earlier catalogue placement does not determine ultimate historical priority. The wider public literature lookup yielded no usable evidence and the Devillers–Hall full text was not inspected; neither limitation affects the exact archive match.
